steps.title: Choose Your Door
steps.challenge: Choose one goal, one constraint, one next action, and one observable change. Name one choice you do not delegate.
steps.teach: Ask another learner what they want to learn before introducing a framework.

steps.title: Preserve the Before and After
steps.challenge: Compare two revisions and identify change, preservation, and one unsupported inference.
steps.teach: Show why preserving a failure or predecessor can improve trust.

steps.title: Language, Memory, and Knowledge
steps.challenge: Represent one idea in two carriers and inspect meaning, effort, and provenance changes.
steps.teach: Explain one concept once for precision and once for recall.
steps.boundary: carrier != subject; compact active knowledge != deletion of preserved experience

steps.title: Geometry, Carriers, and Strange Spaces
steps.challenge: Transform a pattern and identify an invariant and a changed feature.
steps.teach: Ask another learner what can and cannot be reconstructed from the transformed object.
steps.boundary: useful representation != physical truth; byte identity != semantic truth

steps.title: Build, Compile, Break, Repair
steps.challenge: Write input -> operation -> observable output -> verifier, then prove one mutation is actually exercised.
steps.teach: Give a learner a bug plus a weak test and let them repair the test first.
steps.boundary: mutation not proven active -> mutation result inadmissible

steps.title: Minds, Models, Agents, and Societies
steps.challenge: For one mechanism, state support observation, lesion/counterprobe, and simpler alternative.
steps.teach: Explain why intelligent-looking output is not itself a causal mechanism test.
steps.boundary: mechanism activity != usefulness != general intelligence != consciousness/personhood

steps.title: Mathematics: Proof, Computation, and Open Problems
steps.challenge: Label one statement PROVED, EXHAUSTIVE_FINITE, COMPUTATION, COUNTEREXAMPLE, HYPOTHESIS, or OPEN and state the next evidence rung.
steps.teach: Present one result and one overclaim; ask the learner to locate the unsupported jump.
steps.boundary: finite verification != universal proof; Hodge and P vs NP remain open

steps.title: Science and the Physical World
steps.challenge: Write raw observation -> comparison -> interpretation and invent one confound.
steps.teach: Ask the learner for a control that distinguishes two explanations.

steps.title: Accessibility, Education, and Teaching
steps.challenge: Teach one concept through UDL why/what/how and let the learner's response change the explanation.
steps.teach: Invite a teach-back in a different representation; do not require imitation.
steps.boundary: diagnosis != robust causal instruction; learner first; nomination != authority

steps.title: Worlds, Games, Art, and Share-Back
steps.challenge: Make something that is allowed to be just fun, then add one optional question someone could discover through it.
steps.teach: Let someone play first; explain only when they want the explanation or it serves their goal.
steps.boundary: play/generation != evidence; game canon != scientific observation

finishRule: The history is a playground with evidence boundaries, not a maze with one correct exit.
